name: StevenBlack hosts
purpose: The base variant of the unified hosts file: advertising, fake-news and malware domains, merged from several upstream lists.
breakage: Nothing that runs locally. A handful of sites that pull a required resource from an ad network can come up unstyled or blank.

name: Dan Pollock's hosts file
license: Free to redistribute under the terms in the file's own header
purpose: One of the oldest maintained hosts blocklists: advertising and tracking domains.
breakage: Same class as any advertising list — sites that depend on an ad network for a script may not finish loading.

name: MVPS hosts
purpose: Advertising and tracking domains, maintained for many years by MVPS.
breakage: Some Microsoft services and telemetry-backed features log errors when their endpoints are unreachable; nothing else in Windows depends on them.

name: URLhaus malicious hosts
license: Free to use under abuse.ch terms
purpose: Hosts currently serving malware, published by abuse.ch from their URLhaus dataset.
breakage: None expected: these are domains Windows and ordinary software do not need. If a domain on the list is a shared host you use, the site will fail to load.

name: Stalkerware indicators
purpose: Command-and-control endpoints for known stalkerware, published as a community indicator set.
breakage: None expected for ordinary software. A short list, so the hosts file cost is negligible.

name: FireHOL level 1 IP list
purpose: IP ranges with a long record of attacks, aggregated from many upstream IP blocklists. Applied as Windows Firewall rules, not hosts entries — the hosts file cannot express an address range.
breakage: Higher than a domain list. IP ranges are shared: a block can cover a CDN or a hosting provider and take a site down with it. Read the count before applying, and remove the rules if something stops working.
